rules/combat.html.title: combat
rules/combat.html.description: Enemy phase <=> player phase :: it's whoever started it first. Turn-order for players is in ascending mental stat value. Encouraged to sit around the table clockwise in that order to make things easy. Action-slots = your limbs. Type: Arm => Arm Actions: Attack/Use Defend Stabilize etc. Type: Movement => Movement Actions: Move Dash Status Effects follow the count + potency rules. Scar system list of combat actions

rules/downtime.html.title: downtime
rules/downtime.html.description: Chunks of non-combat non-roleplay time is spent doing "Downtime Actions" Craft Find Explore Rest etc. Use your skill bonusses on these downtime tasks to determine your effectiveness performing it. E.g. A crafted weapon is guaranteed to do (role) dmg per hit on average w/ it's basic attack. list of downtime actions

rules/stats-and-limbs.html.title: stats and limbs
rules/stats-and-limbs.html.description:
Most creatures have a race or race/class combo that determines their base stats & limbs. When creating a character, select a race and class from the list of playable races. This race and class combination defines most of your stats for you. See the following guide for all stats to calculate them. Physical ( determined by race and class ) Mental ( determined by race and class ) Defensive ( determined by race and class ) Effort ( 5 ) * You may select one main stat (Physical, Mental, Defensive) to increase by 1 point during character creation. These 3 stats in addition to the effort stat are used to perform combat actions. (New characters start at 5 effort.) Vitality has 3 parts to notate. Current Vitality, Maximum Vitality, and Attuned Vitality. Maximum Vitality is calculated by summing the vitality of your limbs. Current Vitality and Attuned Vitality both start equal to your maximum. Cur Vitality ( determined by race and class ) Max Vitality ( determined by race and class ) Att Vitality ( determined by race and class ) Choose any 3 items from their loot tables to start off with, write these items in your "possessions". These items can include armor. Your armor stat is whatever is listed on your armor. This armor value is the ratio of defensive effort spent to amount of damage reduced. When unarmored or in standard clothing, your armor stat is equal to the 'toughness' determined by your race. Armor ( determined by your equipped armor ) Limbs determine two things: maximum vitality and action slots. Each limb is formatted like the template below, showing the maximum vitality increase and the types of actions it can perform. Something's Appendage. [+3 MV] [Type] - Any custom action(s) this limb can perform.
During your combat turns, you will iterate through your action slots provided by your limbs, spending "effort" to perform an action of that type or one explicitly listed by the limb.
Now you are prepared for combat. Now just read to combat rules to learn how to roll the dice.
Read story and skills to learn everything you need to know about downtime.

rules/story-and-skills.html.title: story and skills
rules/story-and-skills.html.description: A creature's story summarizes chapters of useful and pivotal experiences into "Cantos". Each Canto signifies a great deal of time, effort, and survival. As such, select 4 skills to gain or specialize in as a result of these experiences. Make sure to choose the proper skills that match your character's experiences and feats. These skills are used in "downtime actions" and roleplay. A new player-character must select a background to start their story.

info_showOrphanNodes.description: Show nodes that are not connected to any other nodes.

info_showAttachments.description: Show attachments like images and PDFs as nodes in the graph.

info_allowGlobalGraph.description: Allow the user to view the global graph of all nodes.

info_allowExpand.description: Allow the user to pop-out the graph view to take up the whole screen

info_attractionForce.description: How much should linked nodes attract each other? This will make the graph appear more clustered.

info_linkLength.description: How long should the links between nodes be? The shorter the links the more connected nodes will cluster together.

info_repulsionForce.description: How much should nodes repel each other? This will make disconnected parts more spread out.

info_centralForce.description: How much should nodes be attracted to the center? This will make the graph appear more dense and circular.

info_edgePruning.description: Edges with a length above this threshold will not be rendered, however they will still contribute to the simulation. This can help large tangled graphs look more organised. Hovering over a node will still display these links.

info_minNodeRadius.description: How small should the smallest nodes be? The smaller a node is the less it will attract other nodes.

info_maxNodeRadius.description: How large should the largest nodes be? Nodes are sized by how many links they have. The larger a node is the more it will attract other nodes. This can be used to create a good grouping around the most important nodes.
